title: Why Does the Moon Change Shape?
logline: Pipi thinks someone is eating the Moon. Bravo proves it is still a ball — we just see different slices of sunlight as it orbits Earth.
moral: The Moon does not shrink. Its shape changes because of sunlight and our point of view.
tone: Gentle STEM explainer for ages 6–7. Lab host + 2D screen graphics. Only Bravo and Pipi.

characters.name: Bravo
characters.blurb: Explains the Moon with gadgets, a flashlight, and a ball. Patient, curious, never condescending.

characters.name: Pipi
characters.blurb: Asks the kid questions out loud. Beeps, points, learns with the audience.

locations.name: Secret lab
locations.note: Entire episode. Big wall screen carries the 2D lesson graphics.

scenes.heading: SCENE 01  INT. BRAVO'S SECRET LAB - NIGHT

blocks.text: The secret lab glows teal. On the big curved WALL SCREEN: a cute flat drawing of a full Moon. BRAVO (civilian) sits at the work table with a flashlight and a white foam ball. PIPI hovers beside him, staring at the screen.
(worried beep)
Alert. The Moon is broken. Last week: big circle. Tonight: tiny smile. Someone is eating it.
(grinning, gentle)
Nobody is eating the Moon, Pipi. But it DOES look like it changes shape. Want to know why?
Yes. Science snack. Go.
Bravo taps the console. Title card blooms on the wall screen in soft 2D: WHY DOES THE MOON CHANGE SHAPE?

scenes.heading: SCENE 02  INT. LAB / DEMO TABLE - CONTINUOUS

blocks.text: Bravo holds up the white ball. Pipi clicks on a tiny desk lamp / flashlight. On the WALL SCREEN, a matching 2D cartoon ball and sun-lamp appear.
First big secret: the Moon is a ball. A giant rocky ball floating in space. It does not shrink. It does not melt.
(poking the foam ball)
Ball confirmed. Squishy version is smaller.
Second secret: the Moon does not make its own light. The Sun lights it up. Like this.
He shines the flashlight on one side of the ball. Half bright, half dark. The screen mirrors it in clean 2D: yellow sun rays hitting a grey moon-ball.
Ooooh. One cheek sunny. One cheek sleepy.

scenes.heading: SCENE 03  INT. LAB / WALL SCREEN - CONTINUOUS

blocks.text: Bravo walks the ball in a slow circle around a little stand labeled EARTH (or Pipi herself as Earth). Camera favors the WALL SCREEN as the lesson takes over in 2D.
We live on Earth. The Moon travels around us. As it moves, we see different sunny pieces of that ball.
ON SCREEN (2D): Earth in the middle. Sun fixed on the left. Moon slides around Earth. A little eye-icon shows what Earth kids see each time.
When the sunny side faces us — we see a FULL MOON. A bright circle.
Big cookie.
When we mostly see the dark side — almost no cookie. That is a NEW MOON. The Moon is still there. It is just hiding in the Sun's shadow from our view.
(relieved)
Not eaten. Just sneaky.

scenes.heading: SCENE 04  INT. LAB / PHASE PARADE ON SCREEN - CONTINUOUS

blocks.text: The wall screen becomes a cheerful PHASE PARADE — five big moon shapes slide left to right. Bravo points with a laser pointer; Pipi zooms along the row.
In between, we get shapes with funny names. Like a banana. That is a CRESCENT.
Moon banana. Do not eat.
Half lit is a HALF MOON. And when it is almost full, we call it a GIBBOUS — which just means 'bumpy almost-circle.'
ON SCREEN (2D): New → Crescent → Half → Gibbous → Full, then reverse. A tiny calendar note: about one month for a full trip.
The whole show takes about one month. Same Moon. Same ball. Different sunny slice for our eyes.
Shape change equals view change. Download complete.
Bravo kills the flashlight. The foam ball sits in soft lab light — always a full sphere. The screen shows a quiet night sky with a crescent and a tiny label: STILL A BALL.
So next time you look up and the Moon looks skinny, remember: it did not shrink. You are just seeing a different piece of sunlight.
(to camera / kids, soft)
Tonight homework: find the Moon. Ask: banana, half, or cookie?
Great question, Pipi. And a great sky. Widgeteers Explains — mystery solved.
Pipi draws a tiny teal heart on the screen over the Moon. Bravo clicks off the title. Soft fade.
THE END
